candidates.title: 10 great witch films
candidates.excerpt: From silent-era demons to modern folk-horror nightmares, witches have haunted cinema for well over a century. These 10 films chart the evolution of the screen witch, revealing how ideas about female power, fear and otherness have been transformed across cultures and generations.

candidates.title: Cannes winner Everytime coming to UK and Irish cinemas on 26 February
candidates.excerpt: Sandra Wollner’s third feature, the enigmatic Un Certain Regard prize-winner will open in UK and Irish cinemas through BFI Distribution.

candidates.title: Kiss kiss bang bang: Baz Luhrmann’s Romeo + Juliet
candidates.excerpt: For the 30th anniversary of Baz Luhrmann’s visceral epic Romeo + Juliet, we republish José Arroyo’s essay on how the film turned Shakespeare into cinema. From our March 1997 issue.

candidates.title: The world moves on: Billy Wilder’s cinema of ageing and obsolescence
candidates.excerpt: From overlooked office workers to fading movie stars, ageing in Billy Wilder’s films is about more than growing old. Across his career, he wittily chronicled characters confronting missed opportunities, diminished relevance and the feeling that life has passed them by.

candidates.title: Wildwood: Laika’s ambitious fantasy shows off its spellbinding stop motion craft
candidates.excerpt: Laika animation studio’s film about a teen on an epic quest to save her baby brother is filled with astounding detail, but the magic lies in the craftsmanship rather than the story.

candidates.title: BFI Player’s November 2026 line-up
candidates.excerpt: Settle into November with a feast of cinema, from the splendour of silent classics to bold new voices and rare discoveries.

candidates.title: Scotland’s rival to The Jazz Singer: the story behind a groundbreaking British sound film
candidates.excerpt: One hundred years after its Edinburgh cinema release, we tell the story behind Till the Bells Ring, a Scottish talking picture that included synchronised dialogue a full year before Hollywood’s own coming of sound.

candidates.title: Sight and Sound: the December 2026 issue
candidates.excerpt: On the cover: Godzilla, from Gojira to Minus Zero: an interview with director Yamazaki Takashi, plus a look at the monster’s 70 years in film Inside: as the fifth anniversary of the Black Film Bulletin closes, its editors look back on the cultural changes witnessed since the publication began, Diane

candidates.title: 10 great East African films
candidates.excerpt: As this year’s Film Africa opens with Cannes prizewinner Ben’Imana, we explore 10 films that reveal the richness, diversity and transnational currents of East African cinema, challenging perceptions along the way.

candidates.title: Whalefall: Austin Abrams gives it his all in a passable film about a man swallowed by a whale
candidates.excerpt: Brian Duffield’s CGI-filled blockbuster production has moments spectral of sci-fi beauty behind the blubber, but can’t quite capture the evocative prose of Daniel Krauss’s source novel.

candidates.title: Nightborn: Finnish myths are lost in the thicket of this gory post-partum horror
candidates.excerpt: Director Hanna Bergholm’s monstrous exploration of new parenthood ends up feeling overstuffed writes George Townsend, one of the critics on this year’s LFF Critics Mentorship Programme.

candidates.title: Portrait of a lady: Sofia Coppola’s Marie Antoinette
candidates.excerpt: With The Making of Marie Antoinette arriving in cinemas this week, we revisit Pam Cook’s analysis of Sofia Coppola’s irreverent teen queen biopic. From our November 2006 issue.

candidates.title: “It was a way of understanding my own generation”: Manuela Martelli on her snowbound Chilean drama The Meltdown
candidates.excerpt: The award-winning director of 1976 talks to us about her second feature, a wintry coming-of-age drama set during Chile’s uneasy transition to democracy.

candidates.title: Inside the Archive #77: Preserving Frankenstein, a new-look study store and a trip to Colorado via London
candidates.excerpt: This month, learn more about how we're preserving Guillermo del Toro’s latest creation, how funding is helping us transform vital archive facilities and a recent Colorado collaboration with actress Rebecca Hall.

candidates.title: Mahershala Ali on Your Mother Your Mother Your Mother and the impact of representation
candidates.excerpt: The two-time Oscar winner joined us for an LFF Screen Talk to discuss the cost of acclaim, portraying a Black father, and the challenge of finding fully realised roles now he's stepping up to play leading men.

candidates.title: Where to begin with Billy Wilder
candidates.excerpt: As our season dedicated to Billy Wilder gets under way, we plot a beginner’s path through the bittersweet comedies and acerbic noirs of one of the most celebrated directors of the golden age of Hollywood.

candidates.title: Competition winners announced at 70th BFI London Film Festival
candidates.excerpt: And the winners are...

candidates.title: Club Kid: an outrageously funny crowdpleaser
candidates.excerpt: Jordan Firstman’s debut stays true to his irreverent humour while leaving just enough room for sincerity in its sweet story of a queer NYC club promoter who discovers he has a 10-year-old son.

candidates.title: Danny Boyle on his tabloid chronicle Ink: “The attention economy, clickbait, the dopamine economy – this is its hatching point”
candidates.excerpt: Danny Boyle discusses adapting James Graham’s Ink, tracing the roots of Britain’s tabloid revolution and exploring how the Sun helped create the attention economy that now shapes social media and modern politics.

candidates.title: Revisiting Pakeezah, Hindi cinema’s great tragedy of desire and entrapment
candidates.excerpt: Years in the making, Pakeezah is a haunting collaboration between a dying star and the artists around her. As a new restoration screens at LFF, writer and filmmaker Nasheed Qamar Faruqi explores one of Indian cinema’s most emotionally devastating dramas.

candidates.title: Robert Eggers on Werwulf and his career in film: “Everybody is a bit of an island”
candidates.excerpt: The director of The Witch, The Lighthouse and Nosferatu reflected on folklore, filmmaking and creative partnership at an LFF Screen Talk, where audiences were treated to the first footage from his next nightmare, Werwulf.

candidates.title: 10 great black-and-white films of the 2020s
candidates.excerpt: Ahead of the release of Fatherland, Pawel Pawlikowski’s latest black-and-white vignette of mid-century Europe, we round up other films from the decade so far which reclaim monochrome from film history’s past.

candidates.title: All Rivers Spill Their Stories to the Sea: Jeanie Finlay’s documentary is a display of community solidarity in the face of ecological disaster
candidates.excerpt: With the help of the charismatic north-eastern fisherman Stan Rennie, Jeanie Finlay follows a coastal community in crisis after a series of mass shellfish die-offs along England’s Tees estuary.

candidates.title: Javier Bardem on Bunker and The Beloved: “I’ve been in some toxic environments”
candidates.excerpt: Whether playing an abusive filmmaker or an architect consumed by ambition, Javier Bardem’s latest characters struggle to see the harm they inflict on those around them. He discusses flawed masculinity, ageing and vulnerability on screen.

candidates.title: Once Upon a Time in Harlem: William Greaves and son preserve a Harlem Renaissance reunion with a marvel of cinéma vérité
candidates.excerpt: Using footage shot by his father in 1972, director David Greaves has completed a fascinating documentary that invites viewers to hang out with inspiring cultural revolutionaries.

candidates.title: Michael Winterbottom on The Trip to the Northern Lights: “Steve’s not worried about appearing grumpy or lonely”
candidates.excerpt: As Steve Coogan and Rob Brydon return for another series of The Trip – this time bound for Scandinavia – we spoke to director Michael Winterbottom about the lines between fact and fiction, TV and cinema, and why it’s difficult to be as prolific as Ingmar Bergman.

candidates.title: Whose side are you on?: Harlan County U.S.A. reviewed in 1978
candidates.excerpt: As Barbara Kopple’s miners’ strike documentary turns 50, we republish our original review of the film from Sight and Sound’s sister publication Monthly Film Bulletin.

candidates.title: Winners announced at the 2026 BFI & CHANEL Filmmaker Awards
candidates.excerpt: Jessie Buckley and Gwendoline Christie joined the jury this year to present the awards to the winning filmmakers, who are selected for their creative audacity.

candidates.title: Life of Jorge Luis Borges: a labyrinthian voyage through the work of Argentina’s best known writer
candidates.excerpt: Director Mariano Llínas’s five-hour documentary reads through the lines of Jorge Luis Borges’s work, digging into his archives to create a playful investigative literary mystery.

candidates.title: John Malkovich on Wild Horse Nine and “the most terrible line I’ve ever had to give”
candidates.excerpt: Reflecting on a screen career spanning Dangerous Liaisons to his Oscar-tipped turn in Wild Horse Nine, John Malkovich argued that a screen actor is ultimately “a figure in someone else’s dream” during an entertaining and wide-ranging LFF Screen Talk.
